subject: Dedicated capacity MAP kickoff: Acme AI — throughput & GPU pool alignment
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acmeai.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.r@acmeai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 07:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity MAP kickoff: Acme AI — throughput & GPU pool alignment

Tom / Sofia — thanks again for the time today. As discussed, I wanted to kick off a short mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align on the Dedicated capacity sizing, acceptance criteria for the evaluation, and a close timeline. High level ask: confirm stakeholders and targets below, and we will iterate the MAP workbook attached (Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx).

Proposed 6-week MAP (high level)
- Week 0: Kickoff & stakeholder alignment (today)
- Week 1: Test plan + data ingestion sample + procurement checklist
- Week 2-3: Load & performance eval on Dedicated pool (throughput/latency)
- Week 4: Regression/quality checks and runbook validation
- Week 5: Contract finalization & capacity reservation
- Week 6: Go/no-go and handoff to ops

Initial capacity targets (please confirm):
- Target steady-state throughput: 100 RPS (sustained requests/sec) with 95th pct latency ≤ 300ms for 512-token responses
- Burst headroom: up to 300 RPS for short windows (≤ 60s)
- Model: open-llama-70B-quant (or comparable) — latency/throughput baseline attached (throughput_model.csv)
- Approx GPU pool sizing (starting point): 8x A100-80GB equiv or 4x H100-80GB equiv with continuous batching enabled
- KV cache persistence for long-running chat sessions (customer needs low cold-starts)

Dependencies we need from Acme:
- Clarify expected query distribution (avg tokens in/out, P95 request size) — sample dataset is fine
- Contacts for security/compliance questionnaires and procurement
- Target contract/PO date to lock a Dedicated pool

Owners on Redwood side:
- Technical lead / SRE: Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwood.ai) — capacity testing & runbooks
- Sales / commercial: Markus Klein (me) — MAP cadence, contract
- Solution architect: Rafael Mendes (rafael_mendes@redwood.ai) — model tuning & cost guidance

Next steps: please reply with stakeholder confirmations and any edits to the targets by EOD Friday PST. If the targets above look off, call me and we can recalibrate.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook, editable)
Attachment: throughput_model.csv (baseline runs)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity MAP kickoff: Acme AI — throughput & GPU pool alignment

Markus — adding a few commercial/procurement notes to the MAP before we send the final to Acme. Short bullets:
- Procurement: standard SOW + reserved capacity invoice cadence (monthly) — Acme should confirm billing entity and PO lead (procurement contact).
- Discounts: list price holds for 90 days post-commit; for pools ≥ $50k/month we can discuss a pilot discount.
- SLA exceptions: we will need explicit SLA addendum if they require <1s p99 for large responses.
- Security: request Acme's security contact for SOC2 evidence exchange. We will add a secure S3 share link for redacted logs if needed.

I also noted the GPU sizing — Rafael/Dev, can you quickly sanity-check the 8x A100 suggestion vs our continuous batching assumption? If we expect larger sequence lengths (>=1024) we should propose a slightly bigger pool or prioritize H100 for memory headroom.

Thanks — looping you both so we can finalize before I send the MAP doc to Acme.

— Lauren
Director, Growth Ops
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Markus / team — thanks for the clear plan. Quick confirmation from Acme:

Our initial use case is large-batch document summarization for enterprise search, average response length ~420 tokens, P95 around 1,100 tokens for long docs. Expect traffic to ramp over the pilot; initial steady-state target we can validate at 75 RPS and aim to scale to 150 RPS within the pilot window.
- Security contact: Sofia Ramos (sofia.r@acmeai.com) — she'll coordinate SOC2 and network requirements.
- Procurement: procurement@acmeai.com is the PO lead; target for contract/PO is end of March if tests go well.

A couple of asks for Redwood:
1) Can you include a short-run benchmark for 1,100 token outputs in the throughput_model.csv? That will help us tune the pool sizing.
2) Can you confirm whether the KV cache is backed to customer-managed storage when requested (we have compliance constraints)?

Happy to hop on a 30m call if useful — Tom

Thanks all — quick technical notes after looking at their expected token sizes and ramp plan:
- For 1,100-token P95 responses we'll need to adjust memory headroom; recommend H100-class hardware or A100s with aggressive quantization and offload tuned. Proposal: start with 6x H100-80GB equiv (conservative) or 12x A100-80GB equiv if they prefer A100.
- Continuous batching should be configured with a maximum batch latency budget of 120ms and a soft batch-size cap — this preserves p95 SLAs while still getting batching efficiency.
- KV cache can be backed to customer-managed S3 with envelope encryption; we'll surface a managed KMS integration step in the MAP workbook. Acme will need a KMS ARN and a small connectivity checklist.
- I'll prepare a short 1,100-token benchmark run and add results to throughput_model.csv by EOD today.

I'll also draft exact test scripts and runbook steps for Weeks 2-3 (load harness, scripted regressions, smoke checks) and paste them into the MAP workbook. If procurement wants a sample SOW, Lauren, I can attach a baseline template.

— Dev
